summary.text: Karen Spilka is a Democratic state senator representing the Middlesex and Norfolk District and has served as Senate president since July 2018; she is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election.
Ballotpedia lists her tenure in the State Senate as beginning in 2005, and she worked as a social worker, small business owner, and attorney.

paragraphs.text: Karen Spilka was born in 1953 in New York, New York.
She received a bachelor's degree in social work from Cornell University and a J.D. from Northeastern University School of Law, and she worked as a social worker, small business owner, and attorney.
Spilka served as chair and vice-chair of the Ashland School Committee and as a member of Ashland's Democratic Town Committee, Fiscal Affairs Committee, Charter Review Committee, and Personnel Board.
She served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives from 2001 to 2002, filling a midterm vacancy, and was first elected to the State Senate in 2004.
The State Senate elected her Senate president on July 26, 2018.

According to Spilka's official biography as summarized by Ballotpedia, her priorities as Senate president included the chamber's response to COVID-19, the Student Opportunity Act, a police reform bill, legislation to transition from fossil fuels, and efforts to increase accessibility to mental health care.
